noteEn: The nights are long now. Next week brings {ko:동지}, the day with the longest night and the shortest day of the year.

sources.title: 어린이민속사전: 동지
sources.publisher: National Folk Museum of Korea (국립민속박물관) — 어린이박물관 어린이민속사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: "동지는 24절기 중 스물두 번째 절기로 일 년 중에서 밤이 가장 길고 낮이 가장 짧은 날입니다." / "그래서 옛날 사람들은 동지를 새해의 시작으로 여겼고 ‘아세(亞歲)’라고 불렀습니다." / "아세는 ‘작은 설’이라는 뜻입니다." / "동지에는 ‘팥죽’을 만들어 먹고, ‘새해 달력’을 선물합니다."

sources.title: 2026년 달력자료: 24절기

notes: Pass 1, author (content-skill): note, items and sources written from the cited pages, all accessed 2026-10-30; every claim is quoted in quoteOrLocator.

Pass 2, three checkers. Language: romanization of every item and token is the F-CNT-002 converter's output (checked by the build); polite 해요 register in the ko text; Pre-A1 English. Culture and facts: each claim matched to an allowlisted source (§6.6) with the §5.1 conventions. The longest night and shortest day is the National Folk Museum of Korea's own sentence; the date (22 December 2026, the next week) is from the KASI table. 달 is also the word for a month; the gloss names the moon. Learning design: 5 items, at most 8 new (lesson-new-load), no two items of the drop said alike (dictation-unambiguous), no %, score, age word, speaking line or emoji (review-copy).

Pass 3, reviser and third pass: fixes of pass 2 applied (wording kept plain, every holiday and term date re-read against the KASI table), es and ko overlays re-read against the English; no copy claims native-speaker or expert review.
